title: .revloop.json
description: Project configuration for revloop. Every field is optional; anything absent is auto-detected and shown in the resolved-configuration table with source=detected. Every key here has a consumer in procedures/remote-loop.md or procedures/local-loop.md — a key with no consumer is a promise the procedure does not keep, so it is removed rather than left in place. THAT RULE IS WHY THIS FILE NO LONGER DEFINES REVIEWERS. It once carried a reviewers map, and no procedure reads one now: a built-in command names a definition this plugin ships, and a custom command takes one the operator names with --config <path>. A map nothing loads would be exactly the promise this sentence refuses. The format did not die with the key — it is schema/reviewer.schema.json, and a reviewer you had defined here becomes a file of that shape.

version.description: Config format version. An unknown major version aborts rather than degrading.

baseBranch.description: Null or absent: read from gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef.

branchPrefixes.description: Absent: derived from the repository's own commit subjects.

verify.description: Commands run before pushing. Shown in the resolved table BEFORE they run, and deliberately excluded from allowed-tools so the permission system always sees them.

verifyNotes.description: Which CI job the umbrella verify command does not reproduce, if any. The shape of this gap is universal; its answer differs per project and may be empty.

verifiedLabel.description: Label introducing the list of commands actually run, e.g. "Verified:".

trailers.description: {model} expands to the running model's name — the model that did the work, which is the one running the loop. No vendor address is stamped by default. IT IS NOT {reviewModel}, which a local reviewer's command expands to the model the REVIEW runs on. The two tokens are different words because after the local loop's review-model default they are deliberately different models, and that difference is the point of the feature; one token for both would read as a claim that the reviewer and the fixer are the same.

pr.description: The merge method is not configurable: the merge fence sends merge_method=merge, and it takes no arguments so that its command string never changes. Squash and rebase are not supported. CI cleanliness is likewise not configurable — the gate cannot be loosened from a file.

defaults.description: Defaults for the command flags. WHICH REVIEWER RUNS IS NOT AMONG THEM AND CANNOT BE: it is decided by which command you typed, so there is no key to set and nothing to default. A repository that could choose your reviewer would choose which bot login the wait fence filters on and which rungs your acceptance floor is measured against. A flag always overrides its default. --merge, --auto and --accept-at are deliberately absent: this file comes from whatever repository you are working in, and a repository must not be able to turn on merging or to remove the two human confirmation points. A repository that could set --accept-at would lower its own review bar on a checkout you just cloned while the run still reported a clean convergence. Those are settable by flag only, because the flag is the approval. --model is absent for a second and sharper reason: its value is EXPANDED INTO A COMMAND LINE at the {reviewModel} placeholder, so a key here would be the first thing revloop interpolates into a shell command out of a repository-supplied file. It comes from the person typing it, or from the builtin, and from nowhere else. THE LOCAL LOOP'S --no-publish IS ABSENT FOR NEITHER OF THOSE REASONS, and inheriting one would be wrong: publishing is that loop's DEFAULT, so a key could only ever turn it off, and a key that removes an action grants nothing. It stays flag-only because nothing measured says a project wants it, and because the two situations that would — a fork, and a remote that is not GitHub — abort in step 1 naming the flag, which is a louder signal than a default configured once and forgotten. That makes it a NOT YET rather than a NEVER: defaults.localPublish: false would be defensible and nobody has asked for it.

maxRounds.description: Circuit breaker on the number of rounds, for the pull-request loop only. It stays settable from config, unlike --accept-at, because it bounds spend rather than safety: raising it costs rounds and never merges anything.

localMaxRounds.description: Circuit breaker for the local loop. Separate from maxRounds because the two bound different things: a remote round spends a quota and a stretch of wall clock a person notices, while a local round spends tokens and nothing in the room displays that, so the cap is the only brake there is. It is NOT that a local round is quick: measured rounds run 5m27s to 8m39s, inside the remote reviewer's own range, so what differs is what a round spends and not how long it takes. Sharing one key let a remote-oriented value silently raise the local cap, which defeats the only limit that loop has. Built-in 5.
